London's Batman Is Giving Away Free Gas, Coffee, and Hope
8 photos
Photo: Instagram/London's Batman
A hero's work is never done, and Batman can vouch for that. Now that he's not actively fighting crime and preventing villains from doing whatever they're thinking of doing to the good people of Gotham, he's showing up for the people of London.
Indeed, Batman has made an appearance in the last place you'd expect him to pop up, doing things you least expected him to. He's taking his hero duties to London, where he's on a mission to bring back some hope and save civilians one day – and one stunt – at a time.
This reads like a joke, and I'm perfectly aware of it. It's not: there is a Batman in London and he's keeping his identity a secret for the time being, though you can bet your last dollar that he's not Bruce Wayne.
He calls himself London's Batman , breaking cover on social media on September 22, when he posted a video of himself in front of London Eye, announcing that "the Batman is here and the Batman is here to stay." Since then, he's been regularly updating the world on his good deeds, posting videos on platforms like Instagram and TikTok and then seeing them go viral.
Photo: Instagram/London's Batman Whoever Batman is, he's gone viral. And he's about as beloved as the fictional Batman from the comic books, before his fall from grace.
With stunts like the one he's been pulling, no wonder. Arriving at a moment when inflation in the UK is at its highest point, which brings high gas prices and higher-than-ever costs of living, Batman is doing whatever he can to bring some relief to the people – along with some hope.
So far, he's paid for people's gas, he's bought them coffee and gave them cheap meals, he's filled potholes, and he's handed out handheld fans to people on the subway to cool off. Other, sillier stunts saw him help a couple cross the street and sell Freddo candy bars for just 5 pence, as a reminder of how cheap they once were.
Photo: Instagram/London's Batman It would be easy to write off London's Batman as a guy in a rather ridiculous suit (*seriously, how heavy is that thing?!), pranking people for clicks. But at the end of the day, assuming none of the reactions are staged, he's really doing some good. He's also really bringing people some semblance of hope.
One of his most recent stunts was at a south-east London gas station, where he offered to pay for everyone's gas in a single day. The Daily Mail says that Batman actually offered £70 fuel vouchers to people who happened to drive by that day, with costs totaling about £3,500.
It's not like you could bring your entire group of friends, each in their own car, and fill the tank up completely. But it was still better than expected, a gas voucher offered as a gift. "We've been giving hundreds of people free fuel today in London," Batman said.
Photo: Instagram/London's Batman In another stunt, Batman went to Kingston Hospital, filming inside the crammed parking lot. It's always packed to the maximum, so people who drive themselves to the hospital always end up parking in areas nearby and, almost always, getting fined for it. People who need to go to the hospital shouldn't have to worry about parking fines, Batman decreed, heading to nearby streets and paying the fines of those who did get them.
Perhaps the best part is that each stunt is requested by the people. "Tell me your problems and Batman will make them go away" seems to be the Caped Crusader 's new motto, along with "We're trying to bring back hope to London."
Batman has help, not just the financial means to take requests for issues that need solving. When he was handing out handheld fans to commuters in late September, he was assisted by two sidekicks, both of them male, masked, and apparently British.
Photo: Instagram/London's Batman Before that, when Batman declared war to the garbage lining the streets of the British capital, he did so with help with from four mystery men.
He also has help from the community, like the restaurant owner who agreed to sell £1 chicken and chips for several days and the volunteers from the Youth Club who worked with him side by side filling potholes. Whether these people know his identity remains a mystery.
Speaking of the identity of this particular Batman, while we know for sure he's not Bruce Wayne, the Internet seems to believe he's Niko Omilana, a YouTube prankster, former contestant on The Celebrity Traitors , and 2021 London Mayoral independent candidate. Doing a Batman bit would fit Omilana's public profile, especially since he also did something similar a while back, when he set up a fake pop-up store and gave away free mobile phones to protest the rising costs of technology.
Photo: Instagram/London's Batman Omilana, on his part, seemingly has tried to disassociate from Batman , recently posting a video of himself in New York, as if to say he wasn't even in London when these things were happening. The Internet being the Internet, this is actually seen as "proof" that he is the Batman.
Speculation aside, London's Batman is the hero we need, if only to regain hope. To paraphrase one commenter, he might not be able to move properly or fight, but he'll "just pay for everything. Now that's a real hero." Hard agree.
